description: Vectorized NumPy array access for wall vertex attributes.
notes: Rows follow the order of ids(). A corner shared by facets of the same wall is one vertex (wall create vertices stitches coincident corners); separate walls keep separate vertices (wall generate box: 6 walls, 12 facets, 24 vertices).

functions.name: fill_pos
functions.description: Fill an existing array with the vertex location. The array must be the correct shape.

examples.code:
import numpy as np
import itasca as it
data = np.empty_like(it.vertexarray.pos())
it.vertexarray.fill_pos(data)
examples.description: Fill a preallocated NumPy array to avoid allocating a new result array.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
The destination array must already have the correct shape and dtype.

functions.name: fill_vel
functions.description: Fill an existing array with the vertex velocity. The array must be the correct shape.

examples.code:

import itasca as it
data = np.empty_like(it.vertexarray.vel())
it.vertexarray.fill_vel(data)
examples.description: Fill a preallocated NumPy array to avoid allocating a new result array.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
The destination array must already have the correct shape and dtype.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.

functions.name: pos
functions.description: Get a numpy array of the vertex location.

examples.code:
import itasca as it
values = it.vertexarray.pos()

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.

functions.name: set_pos
functions.description: Set the vertex location from an array.

examples.code:
import itasca as it
data = it.vertexarray.pos()
# modify data in place, then write it back
it.vertexarray.set_pos(data)
examples.description: Read, modify and write back pos for every object.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
Setter functions modify model state immediately.

functions.name: set_vel
functions.description: Set the vertex velocity from an array.

examples.code:
import itasca as it
data = it.vertexarray.vel()
# modify data in place, then write it back
it.vertexarray.set_vel(data)
examples.description: Read, modify and write back vel for every object.

notes: Array APIs operate on all current objects of this type and return or accept NumPy arrays with the shape shown in the signature.
Setter functions modify model state immediately.
Vertex velocities are integrated by the engine every cycle (pos += vel * dt), persist across cycles until changed, and enter ball-facet contact kinematics; one call drives a whole deformable wall.
Conveyor velocity cannot be used on a wall while its vertex velocities are active (see wall attribute).
